newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: German remanded on kidnap charges in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: German remanded on kidnap charges in Colombia.

text.p: German Werner Mauss and his wife Michaela were returned to custody in northwest Colombia on Tuesday on charges of aggravated kidnap, conspiracy to kidnap and use of false documents, the chief prosecutor's office said.
The pair were arrested on Nov. 17 near the northwest city of Medellin as they tried to smuggle a person kidnapped by guerrilla rebels out of the country aboard a private charter plane.

In an official statement, prosecutors said they had ordered Mauss, a maverick private detective with close ties to the German government's intelligence apparatus, to be held in the maximum-security prison at Itagui. His wife was being held in Medellin's Buen Pastor jail.

"The chief proscutor's office has ordered (Mauss and his wife) to be remanded in custody without bail on suspicion of being jointly responsible for the crimes of aggravated kidnap, together with the crimes of conspiracy to kidnap and use of false documents," the statement read. It referred to the couple by three of their multiple aliases, Sedel, Schroeder and Moellner.

The capture of the duo sparked political uproar in Colombia. The authorities accused the couple of being international advisers to the National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrilla group or mercenaries who negotiated the release of kidnap victims in return for a cut of the ransom.

The German government maintains Mauss was on a humanitarian mission to rescue Brigitte Schoene, the German wife of a former BASF Chemicals executive abducted by National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels on Aug. 15. Bonn said it gave its full backing to such efforts, even if they were carried out by unconventional means.
Mauss and his wife were arrested with thousands of dollars of high-tech communications equipment and a series of passports issued under different names.

Last week, German TV broadcast footage in which Mauss appeared to have close ties with the ELN leadership. It has also emerged that Mauss was acting as a go-between for Bernd Schmidbauer, Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coordinator of intelligence services, and the Colombian government to set up German-brokered peace talks with Colombia's leftist guerrillas.
